s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness in a pregnant woman with fever, cough, and sore throat, complicated by respiratory distress and fetal compromise
salient_findings: Respiratory distress with increased respiratory rate and decreased oxygen saturation
Fetal compromise with tachycardia and decreased fetal heart sounds
key_facts: 17-year-old Thai woman, 33 weeks and 4 days into her first pregnancy
Carrying twins with estimated body weights of 1900 g and 2000 g
Initial respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute
Initial blood pressure of 130/81 mm Hg
Patchy infiltrates in the upper and middle lobes of the right lung on chest X-ray
Positive for influenza A (H3N2) virus on real-time PCR of lung and heart tissue

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory illness in a pregnant woman with fever, cough, and sore throat, complicated by respiratory distress and fetal compromise
salient_findings: Respiratory distress with increased respiratory rate and decreased oxygen saturation
Fetal compromise with tachycardia and decreased fetal heart sounds

Carrying twins with estimated body weights of 1900 g and 2000 g
Initial respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute
Initial blood pressure of 130/81 mm Hg

Positive for influenza A (H3N2) virus on real-time PCR of lung and heart tissue

shortlist.label: Influenza pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for influenza A (H3N2) virus on real-time PCR of lung and heart tissue

shortlist.label: Influenza A virus-associated pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for influenza A (H3N2) virus on real-time PCR of lung and heart tissue, and clinical presentation of fever, cough, and sore throat

shortlist.label: Pneumococcal pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patchy infiltrates in the upper and middle lobes of the right lung on chest X-ray, and elevated white blood cell count

shortlist.label: Pulmonary embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Respiratory distress and elevated blood pressure, which could be indicative of a pulmonary embolism

shortlist.label: Amniotic fluid embolism
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal compromise and respiratory distress, which could be indicative of an amniotic fluid embolism

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including fever, cough, and sore throat, along with the positive real-time PCR of lung and heart tissue for influenza A (H3N2) virus, strongly support this diagnosis. The presence of patchy infiltrates in the upper and middle lobes of the right lung on chest X-ray further confirms pneumonia.

rejected.label: Influenza pneumonia
rejected.why: Too broad, as the patient's condition is more specifically associated with the influenza A virus.

rejected.label: Pneumococcal pneumonia
rejected.why: No evidence of pneumococcal infection, and the patient's symptoms and test results point towards a viral cause.

rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies do not suggest a pulmonary embolism, and the presence of influenza A virus supports a viral pneumonia diagnosis.

rejected.label: Amniotic fluid embolism
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and test results do not indicate an amniotic fluid embolism, and the diagnosis is not supported by the presence of influenza A virus or the patient's clinical presentation.
